## Behavior

Case A is a one-time, forward-only migration of the still-discoverable `/tmp` history into `.ak/dockets/issues/15/migration/legacy-case-a/`. The implementation will first freeze a versioned discovery specification **before the first `/tmp` directory read/stat**. That specification will define: canonical `/tmp` root; an explicit allowlist of project/role filename prefixes derived from issue #15 and amendment 001; recursion, file-type, symlink, and filesystem-boundary rules; metadata fields; stable item-key construction; generic-exhaust classifiers; and the cutoff timestamp. Enumeration then produces a byte-sealed source inventory from those predicates, not from later value judgments.

Every discovered candidate receives exactly one disposition keyed by sanitized source locator plus file identity/digest: `recovered`, `reference`, `excluded`, or `superseded`. `known-missing` is a separate expectations table because a missing expectation is not a discovered candidate. Each disposition records a reason and evidence coordinates. Supersession alone cannot exclude value-bearing reasoning: a superseded decision-chain artifact is recovered or referenced and additionally marked superseded. Generic session JSONL, tool-event streams, build/test output, package artifacts, clones, caches, and reproducible source trees are excluded with metadata-only dispositions unless an authority/decision artifact specifically cites an irreducible exhibit.

No JSONL receives semantic inspection. JSONL/generic event candidates are classified only from frozen path/type/size metadata, recorded with sanitized locator/length and (only through the scanner boundary) digest, then excluded; no generic payload bytes enter Git. Non-JSON candidates may be inspected only from private rescue copies to identify authority, plans, repair packets, typed Receipts, reviews/findings, adjudications, closure reports, and specifically cited irreducible exhibits.

## Owner

- **Migration caller/Apply worker:** owns frozen predicates, discovery denominator, private rescue, selection, declarations, canonical artifact paths, dispositions, and the single migration commit.
- **Recorder:** is used only for caller-designated formal role invocation/Receipt evidence and its existing pre-promotion scan/redaction/admission lifecycle. It is not the discoverer, selector, migrator, committer, or completeness oracle. No extractor repair is attempted.
- **Git:** is the durable byte store. Any exact byte already Git-resolvable is represented once by repository identity, full commit SHA, repository-relative path, blob OID, and SHA-256—not copied.
- **Independent closure checker/reviewer:** binds a fixed post-migration target commit and independently recomputes inventory joins, exact dispositions, coverage, reference resolution, and forbidden-payload absence; it does not reuse the migration producer’s success assertion as truth.

## Red

Before promotion/commit, run a migration verifier against the frozen inventory and staged output. It must fail on any of these seeded or real conditions:

1. a discovered item has zero or multiple dispositions, or an unknown disposition value;
2. a `known-missing` expectation is smuggled into the discovered-item denominator;
3. a superseded value-bearing decision is excluded merely because it is superseded;
4. a raw JSONL/session/tool-event/build/test/pack payload is staged;
5. a promoted external byte lacks successful Recorder scanner output, or raw secret-bearing bytes remain;
6. a Git-resolvable byte is copied instead of represented by the complete verified reference tuple, or duplicate canonical reference identities exist;
7. any recovered/stored artifact lacks source metadata, byte length, SHA-256, discovery time, redaction status, admission reason, and association fields;
8. Judge/Fixer/Coder/Reviewer/Collector or issue #1/#2/#3 lacks an explicit outcome (`recovered`, `reference`, `known-missing`, or justified `excluded`);
9. manifests claim historical completeness;
10. audit target/range is moving, differs from the migration commit, or findings lack dispositions.

The verifier is ordinary regression/acceptance code only if it owns a reusable repository seam; otherwise it is an apply-time command whose behavior is captured in durable closure evidence, not a duplicate permanent probe.

## Green

1. Privately write and seal the discovery-specification bytes; only then enumerate `/tmp` once under that specification and record cutoff, sanitized locators, lstat/file identity, size, timestamps, and source digest policy.
2. Immediately copy eligible regular-file bytes into a permission-restricted, Git-ignored/private rescue root using no-follow/open-file checks and copy-then-hash verification. This rescue arrests volatility but is neither admission nor durable promotion. Symlinks/special files receive metadata dispositions and are never followed.
3. Build the complete candidate inventory from the frozen snapshot. Classify generic exhaust without semantic payload reads. Inspect only rescued non-generic candidates needed to establish the value-bearing decision chain or a specifically cited exhibit.
4. For each admitted item, first test exact Git resolvability across its containing repository. Emit the full reference tuple when resolvable; otherwise declare the rescued external item to Recorder exactly once for scan/redaction and staged small-core promotion. Never stage raw secrets; retain only sanitized derivatives plus a non-secret redaction report.
5. Emit canonical migration records: frozen discovery spec/inventory, one-to-one dispositions, separate known-missing expectations, Git references, recovered sanitized artifacts, redaction report when applicable, and a coverage matrix with explicit five-role and issue #1–#3 outcomes. Include an explicit disclaimer that the record covers only the frozen discoverable universe and makes no historical-completeness claim.
6. Verify schema/joins, SHA-256 values, Git reference reproduction, no duplicate stored/reference identity, no forbidden generic payload paths or signatures, and no undisposed candidate. Run the repository’s declared build/typecheck/test checks without changing Recorder extraction behavior.
7. Create exactly one new forward commit from the apply starting HEAD, titled with the required migration/docs prefix (expected `docs(docket): migrate issue 15 case A legacy evidence`). The commit contains only Case A migration artifacts and any minimal verifier owned by this seam; private raw rescue/config/scratch is absent. Do not amend or rewrite history.
8. Against that immutable commit SHA, run an independent inventory/completeness audit in a clean worktree. Re-enumerate the committed migration records, prove exact-set candidate↔disposition equality, separately reconcile known-missing expectations, resolve every Git tuple, hash every stored artifact, scan the committed tree for forbidden generic payloads/secrets, verify all eight coverage axes, and disposition every audit finding. Preserve the audit report through a formal recorded reviewer/collector invocation only if it can remain in the same single migration commit workflow; otherwise the apply must stop rather than create an unauthorized second commit or falsely claim closure.

## Scope

Included: issue #15 **Case A only**, amendments 001/003/005/006 as converged, private rescue, value-bearing migration, Recorder-backed scan/redaction and formal Receipt evidence, exact dispositions, Git-reference deduplication, five-role and issue #1–#3 outcomes, one forward migration commit, and fixed-target independent audit.

Excluded: Case B mandate-reconciliation design, Recorder extractor/duplicate-envelope repair, Recorder runtime changes, JSONL semantic inspection, generic payload retention/copy, cold storage, history rewrite, amendment of existing commits, and any historical-completeness claim.

Investigation evidence: current HEAD is `94c7138`, clean and a forward descendant of `10365aa`; relevant history shows the prior `ad5f9c4`/Plan-002 reconstruction used the narrowed issue-10 Git universe, so this plan does not repeat that denominator substitution. No files, `/tmp` contents, Git state, tests, or commits were modified in plan phase.
